findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_leaderboards, get_agent_summary, get_address_record, agent_trust_teaser, check_x402_endpoint, seller_check · Private data: get_address_record, get_network_teaser, check_x402_endpoint, seller_check · Public sink: get_address_record, get_network_teaser, check_x402_endpoint, seller_check · Destructive: seller_check.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_leaderboards, get_agent_summary, get_address_record, agent_trust_teaser, check_x402_endpoint, seller_check · Private data: get_address_record, get_network_teaser, check_x402_endpoint, seller_check · Public sink: get_address_record, get_network_teaser, check_x402_endpoint, seller_check · Destructive: seller_check

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "get_leaderboards" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
